pr_title: Fix ActiveStorage has_one_attached when blob or record are not persisted
pr_body:
### Summary

- Purging a not persisted blob no longer raise a `FrozenError`.
- Purging a not persisted record no longer raise an `ActiveRecord::ActiveRecordError`.

Fixes #37069

issue_context.title: ActiveStorage `has_one_attached` not purging attachments
issue_context.body:
I'm not able to purge an attachment using `has_one_attached` and the newest version of Rails.

I was working to update an open-source project from Rails 5.2 to Rails 6.0 and I encountered this issue.

I've created a dummy app with a failing test.

Basically I have a model `Bucket` with a `has_one_attached :image` attribute. I'm able to set the attachment but I'm not able to call `purge` in order to delete it.

I don't know what I'm missing here.

### Steps to reproduce

Just clone the repo:
https://github.com/marclerodrigues/active-storage-not-purging

And run the following commands:
```
bundle install
bundle exec rails db:setup
bundle exec rspec
```

### Expected behavior
Whenever I call `purge` the attachment and its associated blob should be deleted.

### Actual behavior
When I call `purge`, I'm getting a `FrozenError (can't modify frozen Hash)`.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.0

**Ruby version**: 2.6.3
comments:
1. `ActiveStorage::Blob#purge` [destroys](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/3523b9d0096ec0229e9db336f0fb042b17c73978/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L226) the blob record, freezing its attributes.

2. Then it [deletes](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/3523b9d0096ec0229e9db336f0fb042b17c73978/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L227) the stored file... but the uploaded file hasn’t been stored yet, because the `Bucket` record hasn’t been saved, so the blob doesn’t have a key.

3. `ActiveStorage::Blob#delete` [calls `#key`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/3523b9d0096ec0229e9db336f0fb042b17c73978/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L218), which [attempts to generate a key](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/3523b9d0096ec0229e9db336f0fb042b17c73978/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L105) if the blob doesn’t have one already. Writing the generated key back to the blob’s frozen attributes raises.

`ActiveStorage::Blob#purge` should no-op for blobs that haven’t been persisted yet… but can you avoid calling it for those blobs?

Hey @georgeclaghorn, thanks for the explanation!

I can avoid calling it for blobs that haven't been persisted but was this supposed to happen in the first place? Testing with Rails 5.2.3, everything works just fine as you can see in this [example](https://github.com/marclerodrigues/active-storage-purging).

@georgeclaghorn thanks for your explanation. I fixed my FrozenError that I was getting since I upgraded to Rails 6.0 by setting the attachment to nil (translated to this example, I called `image = nil` instead of `image.purge`).
this issue is still open or ??

review_comments: I think this could be an Active Record method - we have `previously_new_record?` for example. However let's do that in a different PR.
Good point, I'll make a follow up PR.

This method sticks out to me, I wonder if we shouldn't be using [Attached::Changes](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/d9749bebf64d26f9afb467ee7bad124ba38ad68d/activestorage/lib/active_storage/attached/changes.rb) interface instead? 🤔

I understand your feeling, I'm just not sure how we could do it: we need to reset the changes which weren't being applied yet (because we are purging the attachment); how can make changes reset themselves?

In https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/d9749bebf64d26f9afb467ee7bad124ba38ad68d/activestorage/lib/active_storage/attached/model.rb#L196-L212 We have already some logic to manipulate attachments, you think adding this method there is more consistent?
@intrip Somehow I missed this, yeah I'm not sure the best place but I was just calling it out incase there was any better ideas. At least it's easy to refactor later as long as the API is private? 🙏
@zzak Indeed: method visibility allows easy refactoring later on, if you agree I'd keep this change as it is for now.

The `attachment_changes` api is definitely a weak spot - if you want to create a validator that checks an image before it's uploaded to S3 or whatever then you end up having to [reach deep inside some private apis][1] 😬 

I'd like to expose that in a better way but that's for a different PR - I think this is fine for the moment.

[1]: https://github.com/alphagov/e-petitions/blob/master/app/validators/image_validator.rb#L20-L39
